fields.why: The health outcome is daily asthma ED visit counts; daily mean PM2.5 is the exposure. A's 'continuous' is defensible because the report makes claims about PM2.5 increases above baseline.
The 1,310 total visits and peak PM2.5 values are single-quantity summaries (B), but no claim rests on them alone, so comparison only (A) is also defensible.
The region-specific correlations pair one monitor's PM2.5 with aggregate daily ED counts per region, so the unit of analysis is a group (region-day): ecologic, inferred since no design is named.
'Extreme weather events might worsen these health inequities' names an environmental hazard, not a social, structural or political determinant, and it rests on cited external data.

brief_issues: Brief could say whether environmental exposures (wildfire smoke, extreme weather) can count as determinants_of_health.
